tasting_note: The California estate of Champagne Louis Roederer, a Chardonnay-led brut with 10 to 15% oak-aged reserve wine for depth. Citrus, green apple, and fresh-baked bread ride a fine, persistent mousse to a dry, mineral finish.

Traditional-method Penedès cava from Xarel·lo, Macabeo, and Parellada, aged ten months on the lees. White flowers and citrus give way to pear, stone fruit, and a creamy, lightly toasty palate that finishes crisp and dry.

A modern Franciacorta rosé of Chardonnay and Pinot Nero, part-aged in barrique for depth. Wild strawberry, rose petal, and orchard fruit lead a structured, crisp palate with a saline, almond-tinged finish.

Glera with a splash of Pinot Noir in the Prosecco style, pale pink and fragrant. Golden apple, white peach, and small red berries ride lively bubbles, with an exuberant, faintly off-dry palate and refreshing acidity.

wine_key: le grand courtage blanc de blancs
display_name: Le Grand Courtage Blanc de Blancs
tasting_note: A French sparkler blending Chardonnay, Chenin Blanc, Colombard, and Ugni Blanc into delicate bubbles. Green apple, honeysuckle, and toasted brioche meet a touch of Meyer lemon, balancing crisp acidity against a gentle hint of sweetness.

A non-alcoholic sparkler in the Italian style, crafted to drink like the real thing. Fresh green apple, pear, and peach with a lift of lime and fine, chalky acidity, finishing clean, dry, and refreshing.
A pale, playful Pinot Noir rosé built for easy sipping. Strawberry, raspberry, and watermelon with a twist of citrus and a whisper of orange blossom, finishing crisp, dry, and refreshing.

A southern French white from the stony Costières de Nîmes, blending Roussanne and Grenache Blanc with no oak. White flowers, apple, and white peach over bright citrus and a clean, mineral, food-friendly finish.

A light, modern Vinho Verde from Arinto, Trajadura, and Loureiro, steel-fermented for freshness. Green apple, grapefruit, and white peach with the style's faint spritz and a brisk, just-off-dry finish.
Mostly steel-fermented with a touch of neutral oak for texture. Ruby grapefruit, citrus, and a hint of fresh herbs lead to melon, fig, and lime on a crisp, mouthwatering, dry finish.

A high-altitude Alto Adige Pinot Grigio, steel-fermented and rested on its lees for texture. Pear, apple, citrus, and white blossom with fresh, chalky minerality, fuller and more structured than most.

A Burgundian-minded California Chardonnay, mostly steel with a small portion barrel-aged. Pear, lemon curd, and ripe orchard fruit framed by a whisper of vanilla, staying creamy yet bright and balanced.

region: Tondre Vineyard, Santa Lucia Highlands, Monterey, CA
tasting_note: An off-dry Santa Lucia Highlands Riesling from the Tondré Grapefield. Melon, honey, and ripe grapefruit with apricot and pear, the gentle sweetness held in check by fresh, lively acidity and a long finish.
A cult California blend of mostly Chenin Blanc with a splash of Viognier, all steel. Honeysuckle, white peach, and citrus with a touch of ginger spice, lightly off-dry but kept crisp and lively.
A rounded southern Rhône white from Grenache Blanc, Roussanne, and Viognier. Apricot, white flowers, and peach with a hint of fennel and almond, fresh and supple over a stony, mineral finish.

From the cobbled riverbeds of Arroyo Seco in Monterey, a crisp, Loire-leaning Sauvignon Blanc. Grapefruit, gooseberry, and lime with a snap of fresh herbs and a stony, almost saline minerality on a bright, dry finish.

A California Chardonnay from the historic Seghesio family, with a small splash of estate Vermentino for lift. Lemon curd, pear, and white peach with just a kiss of oak, creamy in the middle but kept fresh by bright acidity. NOTE: tri-county blend (Sonoma/Monterey/SLO), about 95% Chardonnay with 5% estate Vermentino; menu lists Monterey only.

From the cool Oak Knoll district, an estate-grown Chardonnay known for elegance and bright acidity. Apple, pear, and citrus with a light floral lift and just a frame of toasted oak, barrel-fermented but restrained and notably fresh.

An estate Viognier from a Santa Ynez Rhône pioneer, with vines planted in 1997. White flowers, nectarine, and orange blossom with peach and honeysuckle, medium-bodied and aromatic but kept dry and refreshing by lively acidity. NOTE: menu prints 'Cushion Block'; producer labels this bottling 'Cushman Block'.

A rich, Burgundian-style Carneros Chardonnay, barrel-fermented in French oak with wild yeast and full malolactic. Golden apple, pear, and citrus layered with hazelnut, butterscotch, and toasted oak, lush and full yet carried by bright acidity.

A volcanic Carricante grown high on Mount Etna and raised in concrete, never oak. White peach, Meyer lemon, and pear with white flowers and a striking saline, stony minerality, taut and bright through a long, savory finish.

A benchmark Friulian Pinot Grigio from the marl hills of Colli Orientali, rested on its lees for depth. White peach, pear, and melon with floral and savory notes, fuller and more complex than most, fresh and mineral on a long finish.

A cool, coastal Sonoma Chardonnay in a restrained, Burgundian style, barrel-fermented with a light touch of new oak. Lemon, green apple, and white flowers over a saline, chalky minerality, medium-bodied with firm, linear acidity.

From old Russian River vines first planted in 1959, a benchmark California Sauvignon Blanc, mostly steel-fermented. Grapefruit, passion fruit, and melon with gooseberry and a chalky minerality, rich yet racy with a long, mouthwatering finish.

varietal: Touriga Nacional + Tinta Roriz + Touriga Franca
tasting_note: A dry Douro red from the Symington family behind Dow's Port, built on the great Port grapes led by Touriga Nacional and aged briefly in oak. Blackberry and blackcurrant with licorice, pepper, and spice, full and dry with firm but approachable tannins and balancing acidity.

An unoaked, organically farmed Tempranillo from the high plains of La Mancha, fermented in steel to keep the fruit fresh. Cherry, raspberry, and plum with floral and spice notes, lively and medium-bodied with marked but easy tannins and bright acidity.

An old-vine Malbec from Agrelo in Luján de Cuyo, high in the Andes foothills, with a light touch of oak. Cherry, blackberry, and plum with violet and a toasty hint, warm and rounded with a creamy texture and supple, well-built tannins.

A classic southern Rhône GSM blend (Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre), largely unoaked to keep the fruit bright. Juicy blackberry, raspberry, and cherry with violet, licorice, and a touch of garrigue, medium-bodied, fresh, and silky with soft tannins. NOTE: the widely sold 'Les Abeilles' Côtes du Rhône is Jean-Luc Colombo's GSM; menu source attribution referenced J. Boutin, so confirm producer.

The benchmark Sonoma County Zinfandel from a family growing the grape since 1895. Black raspberry, plum, and blackberry with black pepper, anise, and sweet spice over a frame of oak, bold and richly fruited yet balanced, with supple, dusty tannins and a dry finish.

A Columbia Valley Cabernet from Matthews of Woodinville, rounded out with Merlot and a touch of new oak. Blackberry, black currant, and plum with cocoa, vanilla, and sweet spice, full-bodied and polished with supple, well-integrated tannins.

A Merlot-dominant right-bank Bordeaux from Montagne-Saint-Émilion, raised in vat to keep the fruit pure. Blackberry, cherry, and cassis with cedar, tobacco, and a touch of chocolate, full-bodied and savory with ripe, velvety tannins and a fresh finish.

A classic Russian River Valley Pinot Noir, smooth and fruit-forward with just a touch of oak. Cherry, raspberry, and cranberry with cola, rose petal, and a hint of clove, bright and silky with round, soft tannins.

A small-lot, terroir-driven Pinot Noir from the cool Monterey coast. Red cherry, pomegranate, and cranberry with floral, orange-peel, and dried-herb notes, light-bodied and bright with fine, gently firm tannins.

A volcanic Sicilian red from Nerello Mascalese grown high on Mount Etna, raised in concrete and large oak. Red cherry, strawberry, and raspberry with Mediterranean herbs, white pepper, and a stony minerality, light-bodied and elegant with bright acidity and fine, gently grippy tannins.

A small-lot, cool-climate Pinot Noir from Santa Barbara County, light in color and built for finesse. Cranberry, pomegranate, and red cherry with cola, dried herbs, and a floral, spicy lift, light-bodied and energetic with bright acidity and fine, gentle tannins.

A coastal Tuscan red from Bolgheri, led by Sangiovese and Cabernet with Merlot and Syrah. Red and black cherry, currant, and raspberry with leather, tobacco, and spice, medium to full-bodied and harmonious with fresh acidity and supple tannins. NOTE: this is a multi-grape Bolgheri Rosso (roughly 30% Sangiovese, 30% Cabernet, plus Merlot and Syrah), not a Sangiovese varietal.

A bold California red blend from acclaimed winemaker Andy Erickson, built on mountain Cabernet Sauvignon with Syrah, Merlot, and Cabernet Franc. Blackberry, cassis, and dark cherry with chocolate, leather, and savory spice, full-bodied and plush with ripe, fine-grained tannins.

A classic Châteauneuf-du-Pape built on old-vine Grenache with Syrah and Mourvèdre, organically farmed. Black cherry, blackberry, and fig with garrigue, pepper, and sweet spice, full-bodied and rich yet elegant, with ripe, plush tannins and good acidity.

A classic regional red Burgundy from a venerable Beaune house, light and food-friendly with judicious oak. Cherry, raspberry, and red currant with forest floor, mushroom, and a touch of spice, light-bodied and silky with brisk acidity and gentle tannins.

An elegant, Bordeaux-styled Alexander Valley Cabernet, aged in French oak with the fruit and acidity kept front and center. Black cherry, cassis, and blackberry with graphite, cedar, and dried herbs, medium to full-bodied and polished with fine-grained, silky tannins.

A bold, ripe Paso Robles Cabernet with plush dark fruit and moderate oak. Black currant, blackberry, and dark cherry with cedar, cocoa, and sweet spice, full-bodied and flavorful with balanced, velvety tannins and a long finish.

A crisp, dry Napa Sauvignon Blanc from one of the valley's founding estates, made for freshness. Grapefruit, lime, and white peach with a green herbal lift and a clean, zesty finish that stays bright at the table.

Napa's flagship from a winery that has long championed Merlot, ripe and polished with a Cabernet lover's structure. Plum, black cherry, and raspberry with cedar, toffee, and milk chocolate from oak, full and round with soft, velvety tannins.

One of Paso Robles' best-known Cabernets, from high-elevation vineyards and aged about sixteen months in French oak. Blackberry, black currant, and dark cherry with violet, cracked pepper, and a pastry-crust note, dense and plush with fine-grained tannins.

A textbook Chablis from a family domaine on the region's Kimmeridgian limestone, all Chardonnay and built on cool-climate purity. Lemon, green apple, and pear with a flinty, chalky minerality and a steely, bright acidity that finishes clean.

A Santa Lucia Highlands Pinot Noir from Carmel Valley's Bernardus, grown in one of California's cooler, wind-swept Pinot sites. Ripe red cherry and raspberry with baking spice and a savory edge, medium-bodied and silky with bright acidity and gentle tannins.

A Grenache-led Châteauneuf-du-Pape from one of the appellation's oldest and largest estates, blended with Syrah, Mourvèdre, and the traditional varieties. Ripe black cherry and raspberry with garrigue, sweet spice, and a touch of leather, full and warm with smooth, fine-grained tannins.

A pure Sangiovese from a benchmark estate in Castelnuovo Berardenga, aged in large Slavonian oak. Wild cherry, plum, and pomegranate with leather, tobacco, and dried herbs, elegant and structured with firm, fine-grained tannins and bright, food-loving acidity.

A classic Margaux from a family estate prized for finesse, blending Cabernet Sauvignon with Merlot and aged in French oak. Black raspberry, cassis, and dark cherry with cedar, violet, and a graphite-tinged earthiness, medium-bodied and elegant with ripe, fine-grained tannins.

A Carmel Valley Cabernet from Bernardus, mostly Cabernet with a touch of Merlot and rested in neutral French oak to keep the fruit forward. Black cherry, plum, and cassis with a hint of tobacco and spice, rich yet fresh with soft, ripe tannins and a dry finish.

A flagship Super Tuscan from a tiny Bolgheri estate between Ornellaia and Sassicaia, blending Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, and Cabernet Franc in barrique. Black cherry, plum, and currant with cocoa, tobacco, and Mediterranean herbs, full and dense with velvety tannins and a long finish.

A lusciously sweet fortified Muscat in the Rutherglen style, from super-ripe raisined fruit aged many years in old oak. Deep amber and viscous, with raisin, fig, and date layered with caramel, toffee, orange peel, and spice, the sweetness held in balance by a lift of acidity.

A cask-aged ten-year tawny from one of the great port houses, mellowed in wood to a deep amber. Dried fig, date, and apricot mingle with toasted almond, caramel, and honey, rich and silky across a long, gently spiced finish.

From a house known for its drier, firmer style, a young reserve port deep in color and full of fruit. Red and black berry with a peppery, lightly nutty edge, full-bodied and gently sweet with Dow's signature dry finish.

A reserve ruby built from the finest lots and aged about five years in cask, deep ruby and fruit-forward. Ripe plum, blackberry, and dark cherry with caramel and a touch of spice, full and sweet with soft tannins and a warm, lingering finish.

A lusciously sweet German Beerenauslese from Rheinhessen, made from individually selected, noble-rot Silvaner berries. Honeyed apricot, candied citrus, and dried peach are intensely concentrated yet lifted, the low alcohol and bright acidity keeping it fresh rather than heavy.
Legendary Montilla Pedro Ximénez, sun-dried to a near-black, syrupy intensity. Fig, date, raisin, molasses, and coffee, almost a dessert in itself, with just enough acidity to keep it from cloying.

A Charentais aperitif from a respected Cognac house, fresh Ugni Blanc must blended with young Cognac and aged in oak. Honey, apricot, and golden raisin with peach, quince, and a touch of almond, full and gently sweet with a bright, citrusy lift on the finish.

A red Charentais aperitif, fresh grape must blended with young Cognac and rested in oak. Blackberry, dried cherry, and cherry-pit fruit with a faint herbal edge, soft and lightly sweet, lovely served chilled before or after the meal.

The sweetest, richest style of Madeira, made from the Malmsey grape and aged a decade by the island's canteiro method. Fig, raisin, and orange marmalade with toffee, burnt sugar, and roasted nuts, viscous and lush yet kept lively by Madeira's signature racy acidity.
